Captured from `dotnet run --project hosts/web -- --port 8394 --ship grid` — the WP-1 wrecked grid ship. TWO COHERENT SNAPSHOTS FROM ONE SESSION, and the pairing matters more than it looks.
(1) BOOT (connected at host start): `frame` (deck 0) + `roster` + `decks` + `rooms` + `designs`. Deck 0: 8 rooms. Deck 1: 5 rooms — including 'hold' (roomType 14), the LIVE WRECK, a TYPED room so the client has a label for it — plus 3 sealed halls. Decks 2-7: all halls.
(2) WORKING (deck 1, later in the same session): `frameDeck1` + `rosterDeck1`, paired as THE MOST RECENT ROSTER AT THE MOMENT THE FRAME ARRIVED — i.e. the same sim state to within ≤1 render pass. Do not restate this as 'the same host Render() pass': `hosts/web/GameSession.cs` sends `frame` (:1053) BEFORE `roster` (:1069) inside one pass, so a capture client that pairs an arriving frame with the roster it has already received is holding the PREVIOUS pass's roster. (Nor does `Send()`'s de-duplication of unchanged payloads argue the other way — it means a CHANGED roster is always sent, which is the case that makes the two passes differ.) The pairing is sound because it was VERIFIED, not because of send order: all 8 crew positions in `frameDeck1` agree exactly with `rosterDeck1`, and each crew member's task agrees with where it is standing.
⚠ `roster` IS BOOT-ONLY AND MUST NEVER BE PAIRED WITH `frameDeck1`. Every one of its 8 crew reads deck 0 and task "Idle", while `frameDeck1` draws those same 8 cids on deck 1 mid-dig. A test that drives task-tagging or deck-1 pawns from `roster` asserts against all-Idle/all-deck-0 data: it passes and it means nothing. That is why `rosterDeck1` exists — WP-8's "a working pawn is tagged with its task; an idle one is not" is driven from it.
`rosterDeck1` composition (all 8 on deck 1, clustered in the hold at x25-32 y15-16, which is also the tag-overlap case): 5 WORKING — 4 "Digging out …" (tag DIG) + 1 "Crafting at recycler_1" (tag CRAFT, so the tag TEXT varies, not just its presence) — and 3 "Idle" (no tag). Both halves are load-bearing: the 3 idle crew are what let the negative half of the assertion fail.
`frameDeck1` is still the only frame carrying the wreck's fg bytes 4 (Debris, undesignated) AND 15 (Designate) together: at boot every live-wreck tile is designated, so a boot deck-1 frame has 15 and no 4. WP-2's 'a designated tile renders differently from an undesignated one, asserted on the fg byte' must be driven from `frameDeck1`.
Regenerate: scratchpad/wp8-capture.mjs (supersedes wp1-capture.mjs). It is PREDICATE-gated, not wall-clock gated — it refuses to write unless frameDeck1 carries fg 4+15 and rosterDeck1 has >=2 working crew with >=2 distinct tags and >=1 non-working crew. It also steps the sim to 20x while hunting: E0-2 rebased a dig to 10 sim-minutes, so at 1x all 8 crew are still on their FIRST dig ten wall-minutes in and the roster never varies. Faster, not different — the tick sequence is the same deterministic one, and the boot half of this file re-captured byte-identical across two runs with different connect timing. | (3) devices + items — ADDED 2026-08-05 for the SIDE-ELEVATION plate, which sources compartment fittings from these two ALL-DECK channels instead of from the one-deck `frame` (client/src/ui/ship-fittings.js). CAPTURED AT BOOT from a fresh `--ship grid` host, so they are coherent with (1) the BOOT frame and NOT with (2) `frameDeck1`, the working snapshot. MEASURED, and the asymmetry is itself the evidence: against the boot frame the two sources agree tile-for-tile (57 = 57, zero only-in-frame, zero only-in-channel, zero mismatch); against `frameDeck1` there are 10 ONLY-IN-FRAME tiles, every one a spoil-heap the session produced after the channels were sampled, and ZERO only-in-channel. An older channel snapshot can LACK a stack a newer frame has; it can never INVENT one. So: drive the fitting layer from `devices`+`items` with `frame`, never with `frameDeck1`.
